headline_marked: India Women [[refuse Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi]] after dominant final win in Dubai
headline: India Women refuse Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi after dominant final win in Dubai
summary: India's women's cricket team declined to receive their eighth Asia Cup trophy from ACC President Mohsin Naqvi, mirroring last year's men's final amid strained India-Pakistan cricketing ties.
details: India's women's cricket team, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, refused to accept the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi after their dominant 72-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final in Dubai. The post-match presentation ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes.

Naqvi, who also chairs the Pakistan Cricket Board and serves as Pakistan's interior minister, was present at the ceremony. Sri Lanka's players received their runners-up medals and cheque from Naqvi, but the ceremony for India was abruptly concluded.

This incident closely mirrors the men's Asia Cup final last year at the same venue, where the Indian men's team also declined to accept the trophy from Naqvi. This decision comes amidst heightened cross-border tensions and strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan.

Instead of the official presentation, the Indian women's team held its own brief medal ceremony. Fielding coach Munish Bali presented the best-fielder award, and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia handed an award to Nandani Sharma.

India women’s head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI’s position on the matter. He emphasized that for the team, the tournament was officially over, and they were content with being champions.

Muzumdar reiterated that the BCCI's stand is united and supported by the team, adding that they are proud of their performance and are now looking forward to the Asian Games. He confirmed there had been no update on when India would receive the trophy.

The controversy followed India's impressive performance in the final, where they posted 184 runs and then restricted Sri Lanka to secure a convincing 72-run victory. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur praised her side for maintaining high standards throughout the tournament on Dubai's slow pitches.

headline_marked: [[Gas supply increases, Adani power unit restarts]], but load shedding persists in Bangladesh
headline: Gas supply increases, Adani power unit restarts, but load shedding persists in Bangladesh
summary: Despite an increase in gas supply and the resumption of a unit at Adani's power plant, Bangladesh continues to face load shedding due to reduced production at major coal-fired plants and high LNG prices.
details: Gas supply in Bangladesh is expected to see a slight increase from Monday, and one unit of Adani's power plant, previously shut due to a technical fault, resumed operation yesterday. However, load shedding is anticipated to persist for some time, primarily because three major coal-fired power plants are currently operating at only half their capacity.

The country has been grappling with a severe gas crisis for over a month and a half, leading to a significant reduction in electricity generation and a subsequent rise in load shedding. This shortage has also prevented industrial factories from operating at full capacity, causing widespread inconvenience in cooking and transportation sectors.

State Minister Anindya Islam Amit confirmed that gas supply is increasing as planned, benefiting all sectors including industry. He noted that technical issues at some coal-fired plants are hindering further improvement, but anticipates continuous improvement in both electricity and gas supply over time.

Petrobangla, responsible for overseeing the import of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), stated that the previous inability to boost supply was due to reduced LNG cargo imports. Now, with regular cargo arrivals, the supply is being increased.

Petrobangla sources indicate a daily gas demand of 3.8 billion cubic feet, with only 2.65-2.7 billion cubic feet currently supplied. Today, LNG supply may increase to 930 million cubic feet, boosting total daily gas supply to 2.55 billion cubic feet and potentially easing industrial gas shortages.

Petrobangla Chairman Md. Abdul Mannan affirmed that despite low global LNG cargo availability, necessary LNG is being imported to meet demand. He stated that supply would increase from Monday, expecting a rapid improvement in the gas supply situation.

Domestic gas production in Bangladesh has been declining for nine years, prompting the country to begin importing LNG in 2018 to cover the deficit. A severe 25-day gas crisis followed the fire-induced shutdown of Exelerate Energy's floating terminal on July 21, though it resumed full supply on August 15. However, fewer new LNG cargoes continued to hamper overall supply.

Typically, Bangladesh imports an average of 10 LNG cargoes monthly, but only 15 arrived this July-August compared to 21 last year. Direct purchase cargoes expected in August did not materialize, and long-term contracts from Qatar remain unfulfilled. This forces the country to buy from the expensive spot market.

For September, nine out of ten planned LNG cargoes have been secured, despite multiple tenders and significantly increased prices. These include two from Gunvor (USA) under long-term contracts, two from Aramco under short-term agreements, and five purchased from the open spot market.

The Energy Division attributes the surge in LNG prices to factors like the US-Iran conflict in the Middle East, uncertainties in Qatar's supply, and increased demand from Europe ahead of winter. International spot market prices for LNG in Asia have nearly doubled in six months, soaring from $10-11 per MMBTU in January to over $28 in September.

Adani's power plant had been operating at limited capacity for a month due to coal shortages, with one unit shutting down last Wednesday night due to a technical fault, further exacerbating load shedding. The second unit resumed supply yesterday at noon, and by evening, its output exceeded 1,450 megawatts.
